recognize_zh: 低中倍 H&E 下，中央有一片界線模糊、淡粉紅色的區域，由成群的類上皮組織球（epithelioid histiocytes）組成，周圍圍繞淋巴球與發炎細胞，這是肉芽腫（granuloma）；此圖未見明確乾酪性壞死或多核巨細胞。
features: Ill-defined pale eosinophilic nodule of aggregated epithelioid histiocytes in the center
Epithelioid cells with elongated, pale oval nuclei and abundant pink cytoplasm
Surrounding rim of small lymphocytes and mixed inflammatory cells
Adjacent areas with vacuolated/foamy cells on the right
No definite caseous necrosis or Langhans giant cells in this field
describe_en: H&E section at low-intermediate power shows a cellular infiltrate containing an ill-defined granuloma composed of aggregated epithelioid histiocytes with pale oval nuclei and abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm, surrounded by lymphocytes and mixed inflammatory cells. Adjacent areas show vacuolated cells. Caseous necrosis and multinucleated giant cells are not evident in this field. Findings are consistent with granulomatous inflammation; in the appropriate setting this is suggestive of mycobacterial infection, and acid-fast stains and culture are recommended.

ddx.vs: Histoplasma granulomas may look identical on H&E and require GMS/PAS to show small intracellular yeasts rather than AFB-positive bacilli.
Sarcoid granulomas are typically tight, well-formed and non-necrotizing with negative special stains, a diagnosis of exclusion.
Lipogranulomas contain lipid vacuoles within small histiocytic clusters and lack the sheet-like epithelioid histiocytes seen here.
Hodgkin lymphoma shows scattered Hodgkin/Reed-Sternberg cells (CD30+, CD15+) within the inflammatory background.
